siteTagline: Find your next road race across Southeast Asia
heroHeadline: Find your next road *race* across Southeast Asia
_entityUrlSegment_note: Kept as the singular 'race' to match the URL shape of the previous runsea.run site (/race/<slug>/), which Google has already indexed. Changing it to 'races' would 404 every indexed result.

theme._note: Exact design tokens from runsea.run's live design system (see Races/design.html) -- kept 1:1 so this instance's visual identity doesn't change from the engine rebuild. Every other config-examples/*.json theme is intentionally different, proving the token *shape* (not these specific values) is what the engine depends on.

_listicleConfig_note: minEntities is the floor below which a category x country guide isn't worth a page -- a three-item 'best of' reads as thin and drags on the domain rather than helping it. perRunLimit deliberately drips: ~27 combinations currently qualify, and publishing them in one week looks like a content dump to search engines and is more than anyone will actually proofread. 5/week clears the backlog over about five weeks while staying reviewable.

enabledFeatures._autoPromoteDiscovered_note: When true, a newly-discovered race is published automatically: generate-summaries.js promotes it straight from draft to active once it has real content (never a placeholder). Set false to restore the human review gate (draft -> needs_review, still live, but flagged). Only brand-new drafts are affected; refresh's needs_review flags on existing races are untouched.

sourceConfig._discoveryWindowMonths_note: Rolling coverage window measured from the day each run executes, not a fixed end date -- so the directory keeps reaching a full year ahead every week instead of slowly running out of future.
sourceConfig._research_note: Web-research stage budget. researchPerRunLimit caps entities per weekly run so cost stays flat as the directory grows; researchIntervalDays is how long before an entity is looked at again (what people say about an event barely changes week to week). Soonest-dated entities are researched first.
sourceConfig._review_note: Review-article stage (scripts/generate-reviews.js). reviewPerRunLimit caps how many articles are SUCCESSFULLY written per run; entities with research material and the soonest upcoming date are chosen first, and existing reviews are never overwritten. The workflow ticks hourly but only generates when it's been >= reviewMinIntervalHours since the last published review. NOTE on the interval: the cron says hourly, but GitHub actually delivers only ~4 scheduled ticks a day on this repo (measured 2026-08-05: 6 scheduled runs across 37h, ~84% of ticks dropped). 20h is tuned against that real cadence to yield ~1 article/day -- the first tick that lands past the 20h mark wins, which in practice is 22-28h after the last one. Lower this to publish faster; raise it to slow down. A manual dispatch with slugs, or --force, bypasses the interval guard entirely.
sourceConfig.discoveryConstraints: Only include road races run primarily on paved or tarmac surfaces (5K/10K/half marathon/full marathon distances). Do not include trail running events, off-road ultra-trail races, obstacle course races, or duathlons/triathlons -- if a source page mixes road races with trail or multisport events, extract only the road running ones.
sourceConfig._trustedAggregators_note: Each entry is fetched verbatim, so prefer a deep link to an actual country/calendar listing over a bare domain -- a homepage shows a few featured events, the calendar page shows the whole year. Country-specific entries exist because the original five sources skew heavily to Malaysia/Indonesia, leaving Vietnam, Thailand and the smaller markets underrepresented. worldathletics.org is deliberately absent: its calendar is client-rendered, so a plain fetch returns navigation and zero events, and its label road races already appear via AIMS.

notes: Vertical instance config for 'races' (runsea.run). This file is the ONLY place vertical labels/branding/behavior are read from by shared engine code -- no vertical-specific strings should ever be hardcoded into /src or /scripts. See /config-examples for how the other four verticals (hotels, local-services, courses, event-planning) instantiate the same schema. Do NOT point DNS/CNAME at runsea.run's live production traffic until this engine's races vertical has passed Step 5 review and a manual QA pass.
